question: A closed conducting coil is moved rapidly into a region of uniform magnetic field. Explain why the induced current opposes the motion of the coil. What would happen if the induced current aided the motion instead?

options.A: The induced current aids the motion because it must increase the magnetic flux; this requires no external work.
options.B: The induced current has no effect on motion because a uniform magnetic field cannot exert force on a coil.
options.C: As flux increases, the induced current produces a magnetic effect that opposes the coil's entry and thus opposes motion. If it aided the motion, the coil could gain energy without external work, violating conservation of energy.
options.D: The induced current always reverses the magnetic field and accelerates the coil into the region.
